method.name: DBSCAN
method.reference_url: Ester et al. (1996); eps = 90th percentile of the 5-NN distance, min_samples = max(5, d)

tiles.d: The same limit in every seed.
From all-distant noise to noise between clusters, at η = 0.3.
The aggregate stays high while the smallest cluster is mostly lost.
A single cluster or most points rejected, in every run at the largest overlap.

reading: Hurt by distant outliers, not by noise between clusters: inlier ARI 0.00 when all the noise is distant, 0.45 when it bridges the clusters.
It fails visibly. At σ = 1.4, every run returns a single cluster or rejects most points: a user sees the failure without needing labels. Such outputs appear from σ = 0.4.
Imbalance flatters the aggregate. At ρ = 5 the inlier ARI is 0.98, while the smallest cluster is mostly lost (F1 0.00).

overlap.label: Overlap
overlap.what: cluster spread (standard deviation); larger values make the clusters overlap

anisotropy.label: Elongation
anisotropy.what: anisotropy factor: clusters are stretched along random directions

intra_density.label: Dense cores
intra_density.what: density contrast inside each cluster (dense core, sparse rim)

imbalance.label: Size imbalance
imbalance.what: ratio between the largest and the smallest cluster

eta_int.label: Noise placement
eta_int.what: share of the noise (total 30%) placed between clusters rather than far from them
